meta.title: BI Reconnection: A Tool Pointed at Source After Cutover Fails Silently

views.label: Don't rely on self-reporting
views.note: Every connection pointed at a source warehouse comes from the asset inventory, not the BI team's own list.

views.label: M2M, not a re-issued PAT
views.note: PATs are workspace/user-scoped and increasingly deprecated — a scheduled refresh needs service-principal OAuth.

views.label: Silent, not loud, when missed
views.note: A BI tool still pointed at source after cutover reads stale data without failing loudly.

cards.title: The connection string is embedded, not swappable
items: Every BI tool embeds the source warehouse's hostname and HTTP path directly in the dataset/workbook definition
There is no in-place hostname swap in most tools — rebuild the connection against the target endpoint
Gateway-registered data sources don't follow a workspace migration automatically

cards.title: M2M OAuth, not a re-issued PAT
items: PATs are workspace/user-scoped and Databricks documentation labels them legacy
A scheduled refresh has no user present to complete an interactive OAuth flow — M2M is required
Power BI gateway M2M setup is currently manual; budget explicit cutover time for it

cards.title: A missed reconnection fails silently, not loudly
items: A BI tool still pointed at source after cutover reads stale data without erroring
Stage the reconnection in non-production first and validate parity before cutting real callers over
Retire the source PAT/credential only after every known connection is confirmed repointed
